analysis.investment_thesis: A small-cap IT services reseller with a pitiful 0.36% ROE trading at 21x earnings is the textbook definition of a fair (actually poor) business at an unwonderful price. No discernible moat, no scale, and no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 60.39% signals owner-operator alignment
Debt profile appears manageable for a services business
Operates in a growing IT services sector in India
key_risks: ROE of 0.36% is catastrophic — destroys shareholder value vs cost of capital
P/E of 21x for a sub-1% ROE business is wildly disconnected from fundamentals
Tiny Rs 619 Cr market cap IT shop with no evident moat vs TCS/Infy/LTI
red_flags: ROE of 0.36% — essentially no earning power on equity
Near-zero institutional interest (FII 0.57%, DII 5.89%) suggests serious investors have passed
Recently listed micro-cap IT services firm — unproven public-market track record
analysis.detailed_analysis: The single most important number here is the 0.36% return on equity. I have said for sixty years that the best businesses earn high returns on capital without needing much of it — this one barely earns anything. A P/E of 21 on a company generating sub-1% ROE implies the market is paying up for some growth story I cannot see in the numbers provided. Charlie and I would walk away before finishing the annual report. In IT services, scale, client relationships, and delivery infrastructure matter — a Rs 619 Cr reseller-style outfit has none of the moats TCS or Infosys built over decades.
